title: How to reduce AI costs: 9 ways that work in 2026
summary:
TL;DR. The fastest way to reduce AI costs is to stop paying top-model prices for every step. Turn the effort level down first. In Anthropic's own test, one model solved 87.4% of coding tasks at low effort for USD 0.11 each against 95.3% at high for USD 0.29. Running low then retrying only the failures at high reached about 97% for about USD 0.17. Then cache repeated prompts, batch work that can wait (50% off), give simple steps to free or cheap models, and keep the strong model as the one that decides.

title: The average that mixed two waits
summary:
A single number can be correct and still point you at the wrong problem. We had one: the average time from a checked change being committed to a new running version starting. It was a real measurement, taken from real records. It was also two different waits wearing one average.

One path, two situations

Changes ship along a single path. Only one release can occupy it at a time. When a change is committed while another release is still running, it cannot join that release's snapshot — it has to wait for the run to finish, then for the next scheduled check to pick it up. When a change is committed with nothing in flight, it waits only for that next check.

Those are different waits with different causes. One is queueing behind work; the other is waiting for a clock tick. The average added them together.

title: Google Cloud Datastream pricing explained, with examples
summary:
Google Cloud Datastream charges for data processed, not for running streams: an idle stream costs nothing. The catch is how "processed" is measured. Google notes that a processed byte is an internal representation of the source data, and for most workloads it is 2 to 5 times larger than the data itself.

title: We shipped a free motion design editor for iPhone: KeyCut Mobile
summary:
KeyCut Mobile is out: we shipped a layer-based motion design editor for iPhone and iPad, and it's free.

We built KeyCut Mobile at CRE8NOW as the pocket version of our Mac editor. The trailer shows the app in action; here's what's behind it.

What it is

A native video editor for iOS and iPadOS 18+, written in Swift/SwiftUI. Every film is made of real layers (text, images, video, shapes, overlays, 3D camera) that you animate on a touch timeline with keyframes. What you see on the canvas is exactly what gets exported.

What's inside

  • 128 text presets in 11 families, plus per-letter, per-word and per-line text reveals
  • 150 transitions in 6 categories that snap to the next cut
  • 32 motion overlays (film burn, grain, light leaks, bokeh, rain, snow, VHS)
  • Text and shape masks
  • A real 3D camera with depth of field: orbit, tilt and dolly with your fingers
  • Color grading, blur and blend m

title: ★ Detecting suspicious logins in your Laravel app
summary:
Imagine someone logs in to your account from the other side of the world. If you're travelling, that might be perfectly normal. But if you're sitting at home in your hometown, it's suspicious. Someone might have gotten hold of your credentials.

We've released laravel-suspicious-login to notify users about suspicious logins and let you decide what happens next. It looks at signals such as the browser, location and earlier failed attempts. You can email the user, block the login or run your own actions.
